name: Brooke Smilen

profile.project: With David Selles (Harvard GSD), exploring associative agent network structures to improve the novelty and diversity of generated ideas. Past builds: The Town, a 50-agent environment for hidden-rule discovery and coordination; Tengo, a writing interface visualizing model interpretations; Perci, a visual perception study companion. Sources: https://mitmedialab.github.io/agents2026-brooke/week07/ and https://brookesmilen.com/research/
open_questions: How can agent networks generate diverse ideas without losing useful connections?

items.title: A connection
items.text: The memory lecture offers an angle on your associative agent networks: remembering explored paths could help agents seek out more distant connections.

items.title: Read MemGPT
items.text: MemGPT’s distinction between active context and stored memory is worth bringing into your network design: which associations should stay close, and which should be retrieved only when needed?

items.title: A question
items.text: Could selective forgetting increase idea diversity without making the network repeat itself?

editions.headline: Could compaction erase the surprising idea?

items.title: A different connection
items.text: You marked association coverage as already explored. Try the communication channel: compare compacted messages with full histories while holding model, network structure, and token budget constant.

items.title: A question
items.text: A summary may preserve the main point but lose a weak association. How would you detect whether that lost detail could have seeded a novel idea?
